prophet: The Prophet ﷺ told his friend Uqbah that no one asks Allah for protection with anything like Al-Falaq and An-Nas. (An-Nasa'i.) He also said they are among the best two surahs people read. (Ahmad, Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i.)

The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Did you see the ayahs that came down tonight? Nothing like them was ever seen.' They are 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the Falaq' and 'Say: I seek safety with the Lord of the people.' (Sahih Muslim, from Uqbah.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says 'Rabb' means Lord. Allah made everything, owns everything and everything belongs to Him. So we ask for protection from the One who has all of these.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says this means the Lord of both the jinn and people.
Ibn Kathir says three names of Allah are in this surah: Lord, King and God. Allah is the Lord of everything, the King of everything and the God of everything.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says Allah is the King of the jinn and of people.
Ibn Kathir says 'ilah' means the one who is worshipped. We ask the One who is Lord, King and God to keep us safe.
The book Al-Jalalayn says Lord, King and God each say something more about Allah. The word 'people' is said again each time to make it clearer.

prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said that every person has a companion from the jinn, a shaytan, who has been given to him. His friends asked, 'Even you?' He said, 'Yes, but Allah helped me against him, so he is a Muslim and tells me only good.' (Sahih Muslim.)

One night the Prophet ﷺ was walking his wife Safiyyah home. Two men saw them and hurried away. He called them and said, 'This is Safiyyah.' He said, 'Shaytan moves in a person like blood moves, and I was afraid he might put a bad thought in your hearts.' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, from Anas.)
scholars: Ibn Abbas said: the whisperer who hides is the shaytan who sits on the heart of a person. When the person forgets, he whispers. When the person remembers Allah, he runs away. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

Ibn Kathir wrote a man told the Prophet ﷺ that bad thoughts come to him. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah is the Greatest! Praise to Allah, who turned Shaytan's plan into just a whisper.' (Ahmad, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i.)
Ibn Kathir says the whisperer puts his whispers in the chests of people.
The book Al-Jalalayn says he whispers to people when they forget to remember Allah.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says when Allah is not remembered, he whispers into the hearts of what Allah made.

Ibn Kathir says some scholars understand this to mean the whisperers can be from the jinn or from people. This is like Surah Al-An'am, 6:112, where Allah says every prophet had enemies from the shaytans of people and jinn.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says shaytan whispers to jinn like he whispers to people.
Ibn Kathir ends his book with this surah: 'All praise and thanks are due to Allah, the Lord of all that exists.'
